long_biography.plain_text:
The purchase of Ellerman in 1983 established Sir Frederick Barclay and his twin David as major corporate acquirers. They sold the conglomerate's brewing arm, retained proceeds for further deals and expanded an earlier property business into hotels and other private investments.

Frederick was generally regarded as the more cautious of the brothers, while David was readier to take risks. Their holdings eventually ranged across shipping, retail, publishing and real estate, with relatives and professional managers handling much of the operating detail. Both brothers were knighted in 2000 for charitable services, formal recognition of giving that accompanied their deliberately private public lives.
